glossary.definition: A line that shows how quickly we forget new information over time.
glossary.example: Your story is the forgetting curve in real life.

glossary.definition: A way of learning where you review something again and again with longer and longer gaps.
glossary.example: But if you want to retain the words, use spaced repetition.

glossary.definition: Trying to bring information back from memory without looking at it.
glossary.example: See? You just did active recall.

glossary.definition: To bring something back from your memory.
glossary.example: To recall means to bring something back from your memory.

glossary.definition: To keep something, for example new information, in your memory.
glossary.example: To retain means to keep something in your memory.

glossary.definition: Trying to learn a lot of information in a very short time, usually just before an exam.
glossary.example: Cramming is enough for the exam, but it's not enough for a month.

glossary.definition: Known to you because you have seen or heard it before.
glossary.example: Reading again gives you a familiar feeling.

glossary.definition: A small piece of a word that has one vowel sound.
glossary.example: A syllable is a small piece of a word.

glossary.definition: A group of related words that come from the same base word.
glossary.example: A word family is a group of related words.
